title: The Swells club parades and the unruly second line
summary: He recalls all-day parades for the Swells with second liners who danced and misbehaved.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What about the swells? What were they like, the swells?

But I'm going to tell you all one thing. I've always asked the Almighty God. Because those fellows like Manetta and Phil and Boca and them, they used to tell me these things and I used to deny them. You see? In other words I was wondering that I'm doubting Thomas.
But God showed me. He made me see the thing. And after I seen it, well, I had to close my mouth. I couldn't say a word. Because I never once thought those things could happen, you see? Oh yeah?
Well it's good that it was in the minority of people that would act this way. That's right. What about the swells? You were telling us about the swells. What were they like?
Well that was a club on Claymore Street. We used to play for them, two parades. They used to give a nice parade. But that second line, they asked me about that second line.

That second line you wouldn't want to play no parades. Police there, run them at this corner right there, the first thing you know before you turn around there at the next corner. Follow the band. They'll follow that band all day long. We play that parade from nine o'clock in the morning up until six o'clock at nine. And they'll follow that parade all day long. We'll just take a rest and go and eat. You know what? Go into a place and eat. Then start over again. And there was people following the band. Group, I don't mean one or two people. And they get a kick out of it. And what would they do?
Would they misbehave or would they be good? Misbehave is right.
